name: Tread water for ten minutes
blurb: The most useful water-safety skill there is. Efficient treading is nearly effortless — it is a technique, not a fitness test, and panic is what drowns people who could otherwise float indefinitely.
gear: Deep water and a lifeguard or a competent buddy
steps: Learn the eggbeater kick: alternating circular leg movements, one leg clockwise and the other anticlockwise, which gives continuous lift rather than bobbing.
Keep your hands sculling flat and horizontal just under the surface, palms sweeping in figure-eights.
Stay vertical and relaxed, head back, breathing normally. Tension burns oxygen you need.
Build up in stages: one minute, then three, then five, resting between.
Practise treading with your hands out of the water, which forces the legs to do the work properly.
Learn to switch to back floating when you tire — the two skills together mean you can stay up indefinitely.
tips: Never practise deep-water skills alone, however confident you are.
Thrashing is the failure mode. Slow and smooth uses a fraction of the energy.
proof: Ten unbroken minutes in deep water, calm and breathing normally throughout.
